doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

chapter: Working as a contractor and organist
title: Birdland in Utica and playing with Tina Brooks
summary: He locates Birdland in Bagg's Square, run by Dicky Frank, and says he played there six nights a week at 18 with Tina Brooks and Ronnie Jackson.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah I hear a lot about, well over the years I’ve heard a lot about Birdland. Where was it?
Birdland was in Bagg’s Square in Utica, where Genesee going north with the bridge — you know where the museum —

Well that was generally Bagg’s Square. It’s all torn down now. And Birdland was part of that scene down there with a great little scene. They had a B3. Dicky Frank ran the place and he was a terrific guy. And I played there six nights a week for the better part of a year with the great Tina Brooks, a saxophone player, of all people, I ended up playing with Tina Brooks when I was 18 years old. We had a great drummer by the name of Ronnie Jackson, that was the group, with the B3.
